newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, October 28.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni proposes "a pact to remake the welfare state" in 1997. Government, trade unions and employers should discuss ways to lower public expenditures and anticipate an assessment of the pension reform (all).

* Leader of CISL trade union Sergio D'Antoni in an interview warns the government not to anticipate talks on pensions (which are normally scheduled for 1998), saying: "There are already enough crisis factors between the unions and the government." (Corriere della Sera).

*The government and leaders of the three main trade unions CGIL, CISL and UIL due to meet today to seek an agreement over tax modifications included in the 1997 budget. CGIL leader Sergio Cofferati in an interview says: "Our our answers depend on what (Prime Minister Romano) Prodi will say. But don't talk of pensions." (La Repubblica).
* The parliamentary Budget Commission approved an amendment lowering the 12.5 trillion lire "Euro-tax" by one trillion (Correire della Sera).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says the second-tranche sale of energy giant Eni has been "a success". The government intends to launch the privatisation of telecoms holding Stet in march 1997 (Corriere della Sera, Stampa).
* Commercial banks' rates on clients deposits and loans do not reflect the 75 basis point discount rate cut by the Bank of Italy. (Corriere della Sera, Stampa).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
